hints.title: Average Target and Net Flow Balance
hints.text: Ensure total dress count is divisible by machine count. Calculate the target dresses per machine and the net balance across boundaries.

hints.title: Bottleneck Constraints on Dress Transfer
hints.text: The answer is constrained by both the peak individual machine surplus and the peak net flow passing through any boundary dividing the array.

hints.title: Cumulative Balance and Peak Throughput
hints.text: Compute target average. For each machine i, compute difference from average and maintain running prefix sum of differences. The minimum moves is the maximum across all machines of absolute running prefix sum and the positive difference of machine i.

hints.title: See the blueprint
hints.text:
```python
from typing import List

class Solution:
    def findMinMoves(self, machines: List[int]) -> int:
        total = sum(machines)
        n = len(machines)
        if total % n != 0:
            return -1

        avg = total // n
        ans = 0
        balance = 0

        for m in machines:
            diff = m - avg
            balance += diff
            ans = max(ans, abs(balance), diff)

        return ans
```

complexity.notes: Optimal linear pass calculating flux bottlenecks.
complexity.whyNaiveFails: Simulating individual dress transfers step by step would be intractable.
complexity.spaceTimeTradeoff: A single linear pass tracks running flux balance and peak surplus.
complexity.interviewerExpectation: A machine can send at most 1 dress per direction per move, so positive surplus is a bottleneck along with net boundary flux.

from typing import List

class Solution:
    def findMinMoves(self, machines: List[int]) -> int:
        total = sum(machines)
        n = len(machines)
        if total % n != 0:
            return -1

        avg = total // n
        ans = 0
        balance = 0

        for m in machines:
            diff = m - avg
            balance += diff
            ans = max(ans, abs(balance), diff)

        return ans
